requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The analyzer's member collection in TypeCollector.cs no longer throws on bad key layouts. When a member mixes int and string key kinds, the loop now reports the diagnostic and skips that member (`continue`). Duplicate int or string keys are now checked with `ContainsKey` before `Dictionary.Add`, so only the first member is kept. The same edits are applied to both member loops. The change adds analyzer tests for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types, two execution tests, and a README section on opting out of source generation.
story.why: Issue 2234 says the analyzer stopped working for suppressed types in 3.1.1. The likely mechanism is an exception inside TypeCollector that aborts analysis: either `Dictionary.Add` on a duplicate key, or `intKey!.Value` on a mixed-key member. Such an exception would suppress every diagnostic for the type. The diff does not show any code that decides whether suppressed types are analyzed at all. The fix therefore only works if the regression was really this crash and not a skip of suppressed types.
touches_beyond_requirement: The duplicate-key guards and the mixed-key `continue` apply to every [MessagePackObject] type, not only suppressed ones. For generated types, the generator now silently drops the second member with a duplicate key instead of crashing.
A new README section documents which analyzer rules apply to suppressed types. This is a user-facing statement of behavior.
An execution-test project file adds a suppressed type to that test assembly.
story.confidence_overview: High confidence that the guards stop the `ArgumentException` on duplicate keys, and that the `continue` avoids the null `.Value` on mixed key kinds. This holds for the first member loop, which the tests exercise with properties. The second loop has the same edits but appears untested. Medium-to-low confidence that this is the actual root cause of issue 2234: nothing in the diff touches how SuppressSourceGeneration is handled. The execution test `NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType` checks nothing it claims to check.

claims.text: In the second member loop, a member with a mixed key kind is also reported and skipped with `continue`. No test in the diff appears to exercise this loop; the tests only use properties, and this loop looks like the field path.
claims.requirement_quote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

claims.text: In the second loop, duplicate int and string keys are guarded with `ContainsKey` in the same way. No test in the diff exercises these lines.
claims.requirement_quote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

claims.text: The setup of the analyzer test file consists of usings, the VerifyCS alias over MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer, a doc comment and a `using MessagePack;` preamble. It contains no test logic.

Execution test SuppressedTypeRoundTripsThroughDynamicResolver serializes and deserializes a suppressed type with Standard options and checks both fields. It does not verify that the dynamic resolver, rather than a generated formatter, was the one used.
evidence: named test `SuppressedTypeRoundTripsThroughDynamicResolver` not found in the test run

claims.text: Execution test NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType only asserts that `GeneratedMessagePackResolver.Instance` is not null. Despite its name, it does not check that no formatter was generated.
evidence: named test `NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType` not found in the test run

In the first member loop, a member whose key kind (int vs string) differs from the other members gets the DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys diagnostic and is then skipped with `continue`. This avoids dereferencing a null `intKey!.Value` or `stringKey`.

findings.description: The diff does not touch any code that checks SuppressSourceGeneration. If the 3.1.1 regression was the analyzer skipping suppressed types, rather than crashing on bad keys, then this change does not fix issue 2234. In that case tests such as MemberWithoutKeyIsReported would pass or fail regardless of this change. Confirm these tests failed on the parent commit.

For non-suppressed types, a duplicate key now silently drops the second member from the model the generator uses. If MsgPack005 is not an error severity, or a user suppresses it, the generated formatter quietly omits that member instead of failing.

`continue` skips the rest of the loop body for a mixed-key member, including the formatter-attribute and member-type checks. Other diagnostics for that member (e.g. MsgPack003) are no longer reported.
NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType asserts only that the resolver instance is non-null. It would pass even if a formatter were generated for the suppressed type.
No test exercises the second (field) loop's guards or its `continue`. All key tests use properties.
